actions.action: Preserve product focus; define a removal fallback
actions.mechanism: Stable product identities preserve focus through reordering; a consistent results heading receives focus only when the focused product disappears.
actions.implementation: Key cards by product ID. Preserve the focused control where possible. After removal, focus a tabindex="-1" results heading and announce removal. Never steal filter focus.
actions.check: Reorder a retained product: its control stays focused. Filter it out: focus reaches the heading, never the document body.
actions.risk: Replacing keyed card internals can still destroy focused controls.

actions.action: Separate loading, count, and empty states
actions.mechanism: A persistent visible status provides quick counts; a polite live region communicates completed updates without moving focus.
actions.implementation: Immediately display “Updating results.” Mark the results container busy. On completion, clear busy and publish the count outside that container; show empty guidance only for confirmed zero.
actions.check: Within one second of accepted results arriving, the latest count is visible and exposed. Slow requests never display premature zero results.
actions.risk: Screen-reader speech timing varies; avoid promising announcement completion within one second.

actions.action: Commit only the latest filter response
actions.mechanism: Request sequencing prevents stale responses from replacing newer products, counts, or focus decisions.
actions.implementation: Assign each filter request a generation number. Ignore superseded responses. Commit products, count, busy state, and focus reconciliation together for the latest generation.
actions.check: Resolve three requests out of order, including stale zero results. Only the latest response changes the interface; its count appears within one second.
actions.risk: Cancellation alone is insufficient when an earlier response has already completed.

actions.action: Make product ordering deterministic and explicit
actions.mechanism: A visible sort rule and stable tie-breaker prevent arbitrary movement among equally ranked matching products.
actions.implementation: Use a deterministic secondary product-ID sort. Keep the chosen sort across filter changes. Expose keyboard-operable sort controls; align DOM order with visual order.
actions.check: Repeat identical queries: product order remains identical. Change filters: surviving products follow the declared sort, and keyboard traversal matches the displayed sequence.
actions.risk: Live ranking changes can still legitimately move products; retain focus independently.

actions.action: Expose large result sets through accessible pages
actions.mechanism: Keyboard-operable pagination bounds rendered content while keeping every match reachable and providing predictable page transitions.
actions.implementation: Add labeled page controls and ranges. Explicit page navigation focuses the results heading. On filtering, retain the focused product’s page if it survives; otherwise use the first page.
actions.check: Reach every matching product without a pointer. Retained-product filtering preserves its control focus; removal uses the heading fallback. Announce page and total counts.
actions.risk: Unexpected page changes require clear range feedback; use pagination instead of inaccessible virtualization.

actions.action: Provide direct routes between filters and results
actions.mechanism: Named regions and skip links let users resume browsing without traversing every intervening filter or product.
actions.implementation: Add keyboard-visible “Skip to results” and “Back to filters” links targeting focusable headings. Label the results region from its heading and expose cards as a semantic list.
actions.check: Using only the keyboard, move both directions and continue in logical order. With a screen reader, locate both named regions and hear list structure.
actions.risk: Avoid assigning grid roles unless implementing the corresponding keyboard interaction model.
